newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra says large Swedish interest in Oxis.
newsitem.headline: Astra says large Swedish interest in Oxis.

text.p: Swedish drugs major Astra said on Friday interest in its asthma treatment Oxis Turbuhaler had been unexpectedly high in Sweden.
"Interest exceeds all expectations," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
He did not want to reveal any sales figures.
The drug was orginally approved in Sweden and launched there in the beginning of 1997.
Astra said earlier on Friday it won European approval for Oxis and planned to launch it in Europe in the beginning of the next quarter.
"We hope to start launching it in May," Ternby said.
Ternby did not want to reveal which country or countries are first in line for the launch.
An approval for Oxis in the U.S. is dependant on an approval of Astra's asthma drug Pulmicort Turbuhaler in the U.S., Ternby said.
"We first want an approval for Pulmicort Turbuhaler before finishing the clinical studies of Oxis in the U.S.," he said
"A registration can come one or two years after that (an approval for Pulmicort Turbuhaler). First we have to finish the clinical studies and evaluate them."
